title: Proper base change for arbitrary set sheaves on schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaves of sets on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and the canonical sheaf adjunctions and composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. Fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and properness is [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $X,Y,Y_1$ be schemes over $S$, let $p:X\to Y$ be proper, let $v:Y_1\to Y$ be arbitrary, and set $X_1=X\times_Y Y_1$ with projections $p_1:X_1\to Y_1$ and $w:X_1\to X$. For every sheaf of sets $A$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the map $v^{-1}p_*A\to p_{1,*}w^{-1}A$ adjoint to $p_1^{-1}v^{-1}p_*A\simeq w^{-1}p^{-1}p_*A\xrightarrow{w^{-1}\epsilon_p}w^{-1}A$ is an isomorphism, natural in $A$. No group structure, torsion, Noetherianity, finite presentation, or surjectivity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), full statement; canonical arrows normalized by the sheaf adjunction units and counits.

proof.text:
Write $\beta_A$ for the counit mate in the statement and $\eta_e$ for the unit of $e^{-1}\dashv e_*$. Under $v_*p_{1,*}=p_*w_*$, its other transpose is $p_*\eta_{w,A}:p_*A\to p_*w_*w^{-1}A$. Indeed transpose this arrow first across $v$, then across $p_1$; expand the unit of a composite as $\eta_{ab}=\eta_a;a_*\eta_ba^{-1}$. Naturality moves the units past the counit, and $\epsilon_p p^{-1}\circ p^{-1}\eta_p=1$ leaves exactly $w^{-1}\epsilon_p$ after the square's inverse-image comparison. These are the adjunctions of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] and the composition-unit comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Consequently
$$v_*\beta_A\circ\eta_{v,p_*A}=p_*\eta_{w,A}.$$
On an etale $V\to Y$ and $s\in(p_*A)(V)=A(X\times_YV)$, this says that $\beta_A$ sends the unit pullback $v^*s$ on $V_1=V\times_YY_1$ to the unit pullback of $s$ on $X_1\times_{Y_1}V_1$. The objects on the two sides are identified by their two projections, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), first paragraph; equality of the two adjoint descriptions and its section formula written out

proof.text:
By [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] properness agrees with scheme properness. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] $p_1$ is proper. For either $f:Z\to B$ equal to $p$ or $p_1$, and a geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$, put $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{B,\bar b}$ and $Z^{\mathrm{sh}}=Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}C$. Properness makes $f$ quasi-compact and separated; [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. Hence for any set sheaf $H$ on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, [lem-weil-pbc-sets-pushforward-stalk-strict-henselization] gives a bijection
$$(f_*H)_{\bar b}\xrightarrow{\Theta}\Gamma(Z^{\mathrm{sh}},H|_{Z^{\mathrm{sh}}}).$$
Every source element has an affine pointed representative $(V,\bar u,s)$, and $\Theta$ is pullback of $s$ along the map from $Z^{\mathrm{sh}}$ to $Z\times_BV$ specified by the pointed-neighbourhood projection. There is no coefficient or torsion hypothesis in this cited continuity theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), first paragraph of proof, using Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), degree zero for sets

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], $C$ is strictly henselian, its residue field $k$ is separably closed and embedded in $\Omega$, and the closed geometric lift through $\operatorname{Spec}C$ factors each pointed projection. The morphism $Z^{\mathrm{sh}}\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-strict-henselian-h0], using its residue-field-fibre formulation: restriction to $Z_k=Z^{\mathrm{sh}}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is bijective for every etale sheaf, in particular $H|_{Z^{\mathrm{sh}}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sections-base-field-extension] to the $k$-scheme $Z_k$, the extension $\Omega/k$, and that restricted set sheaf. Restriction from $Z_k$ to $Z_{\bar b}=Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is bijective. Composing with $\Theta$ gives a bijection $\rho_{f,H,\bar b}:(f_*H)_{\bar b}\to\Gamma(Z_{\bar b},H|_{Z_{\bar b}})$. On $(V,\bar u,s)$ it restricts $s$ along $(\operatorname{pr}_Z,\bar u\operatorname{pr}_{\Omega}):Z_{\bar b}\to Z\times_BV$: the factorizations in clause (1) identify this composite of projections, and the unit-composition formula of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identifies the pullbacks of $s$.

source.place: Tag 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk), final paragraph, using Tag 0A3S (lemma-h0-proper-over-henselian-local) and Tag 0A3I (lemma-sections-base-field-extension); restriction formula expanded

proof.text:
Fix $\bar y_1:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y_1$ and put $\bar y=v\bar y_1$. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies $(v^{-1}p_*A)_{\bar y_1}$ with $(p_*A)_{\bar y}$. Combine it with the two bijections $\rho$ from steps 2-3. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $T=X_1\times_{Y_1}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, preserving the projection to $X$. The pulled-back sheaves on $T$ agree by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. To compute $\beta_A$ on a stalk, represent any element of $(p_*A)_{\bar y}$ by $s\in A(X\times_YV)$ at $(V,\bar u)$. The inverse of the cited stalk comparison represents its inverse-image germ by $v^*s$ at $(V\times_YY_1,(\bar u,\bar y_1))$. Step 1 sends this to the germ of the pullback of $s$ on $X_1\times_YV$. Both maps $\rho$ then restrict along the same map $T\to X\times_YV$, with components $T\to X$ and $\bar u\operatorname{pr}_{\Omega}$. Thus
$$\rho_{p_1,w^{-1}A,\bar y_1}\circ(\beta_A)_{\bar y_1}=\rho_{p,A,\bar y}\circ c_{v,\bar y_1,p_*A}.$$
This proves bijectivity of the actual exchange stalk, not only the existence of a bijection between its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), stalk argument; the omitted compatibility with the canonical map is checked on every represented germ

proof.text: Choose one algebraically closed geometric point over each point of $Y_1$, in the fixed universe bound. Step 4 proves bijectivity at each of these stalks, so [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] proves that $\beta_A$ is an isomorphism. For a map $a:A\to A'$, the unit naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] gives $p_*w_*w^{-1}a\circ p_*\eta_{w,A}=p_*\eta_{w,A'}\circ p_*a$. Transposing across $v$ gives the naturality square for $\beta$. Its inverse is natural as well, by composing that square with the two inverses. If $X$ or a geometric fibre is empty, the displayed restriction maps take values in the singleton of sections on the empty scheme, and the same argument applies. If $Y_1$ is empty, the stalk criterion uses the empty covering family. No section was required to exist on a nonempty object; no group law, torsion, Noetherian, finite-presentation, or surjectivity hypothesis was used.
